video_title: The NBA’s Dirty Little Secret: Business Rules Everything — Even How Basketball Is Played

quotes.speaker: Rick Buker
quotes.summary_phrase: Mattis Buzelis's frustration with NBA mid-range shot restrictions
quotes.excerpt: he has been discouraged from taking mid-range shots since joining the NBA
quotes.quote: I had a lengthy discussion with a current NBA assistant coach about Chicago Bulls forward Mattis Buzelis, saying recently that he has been discouraged from taking mid-range shots since joining the NBA, and how it has negatively impacted his overall effectiveness.

quotes.speaker: Rick Buker
quotes.summary_phrase: Mattis Buzelis's struggle with mid-range shot restrictions
quotes.excerpt: he hasn't been allowed to shoot mid-range jumpers his first two years in the NBA
quotes.quote: Chicago Bulls forward Mattis Buzelis, who is entering his third year in the league, told Vince Carter and Tracy McGrady on their podcast that he hasn't been allowed to shoot mid-range jumpers his first two years in the NBA. That is news that makes me sad. Sad because he is not alone. Sad because if we don't trust a lottery pick who was shot 50% from 16 feet out to the three-point arc through his first two seasons on a team that could use every advantage it can find to scratch into the playoffs, who is going to have permission to utilize all three levels of scoring?

quotes.speaker: Rick Buker
quotes.summary_phrase: Caitlin Clark's offensive development and Kelsey Mitchell's performance
quotes.excerpt: Caitlin Clark is playing the best basketball I've ever seen her play right now
quotes.quote: Caitlin Clark is playing the best basketball I've ever seen her play right now. Her defense has improved and her orchestration of the Fever's offense is next level. Her ability to get teammates easy buckets while still getting her own has never been better. I in no way mean this to be demeaning to her teammate Kelsey Mitchell who is also playing extremely well. But Stephen A. Smith's assertion a few weeks ago that Kelsey is better than Caitlin is proof positive that Stephen A. doesn't watch the WNBA.

quotes.speaker: Rick Buker
quotes.summary_phrase: Don Nelson's early use of analytical shot selection
quotes.excerpt: Don Nelson used the breakdown of where each and every player shot the best from
quotes.quote: The late Don Nelson, who was a Maverick well before he became an actual Dallas Maverick, used the breakdown of where each and every player shot the best from on the floor. He was one of the early proponents of up-tempo small ball, but he didn't insist on a strict diet of layups and three-pointers. Instead, he had a breakdown of the area or areas on the floor where every player shot the highest percentage and told them that when they were in that area and had an open shot, they were to take it.

quotes.speaker: Rick Buker
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson's rigid substitution patterns in Brooklyn
quotes.excerpt: Kenny Atkinson was literally given a preset substitution pattern based on the analytical profile of his bench players
quotes.quote: When Kenny Atkinson was the Brooklyn Nets head coach, he was literally given a preset substitution pattern based on the analytical profile of his bench players. I don't know if Atkinson has always been a hardcore analytics believer or he realized following them is the best way to get and keep a job, but he is apparently all in now. This is the same Atkinson who said in last year's conference finals against the Knicks that while his Cavs were down in the series three games to none, analytically they were actually ahead in the series 2-1. That is essentially saying winning is not the be-all and end-all. It is equally important to play analytically smart basketball.
